text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Eight Libyan prisoners at Malta's jail, in statement sent to newspapers, say a two-year-old agreement providing for them to serve the rest of their terms in Libya should be respected. In reaction, the Maltese government said five of the prisoners were not eligible for transfer and of the remaining three, only one had asked to go to Libya. His case was being considered.

- Mid-Med Life Assurance, a subsidiary of Mid-Med Bank, reported losses of $625,836 for the first 17 months since its formation until last December. These, it said, were in line with projections and the future looked good.
- Malta celebrates Workers' Day with political parties planning to hold large public rallies on Thursday, a public holiday.
- Maltese soccer hits rock bottom after 2-1 defeat by Faroe Islands in a World Cup match in Malta on Wednesday.
- Six-year-old boy in danger of dying after road accident.
- Archbishop Mgr Joseph Mercieca insists value of work cannot be calculated only in monetary terms. He made his remarks at a mass for workers on Wednesday to mark the feast of St Joseph, the worker.
